Incident Name: Port of Houston Sulfuric Acid Tanker Leak
4 MapSketch include sketch showing the t: North-oriented map of a 2.5-mile radius centered on Berth 42 of the Houston Ship Channel Tank Terminal. The primary site is Tanker Berth 42, MM 51.2 on the West Bank, where a manifold failure aboard M/T Stolt Synergy released 98% sulfuric acid onto the deck and secondary containment, with runoff entering the waterway. A 500-yard berth perimeter has localized water discoloration and acidic mist extending 400 yards downwind. Threatened areas are San Jacinto Battleground Historic Site 1.2 miles down-river and Channelview Residential Neighborhood 2.0 miles North-Northwest. USCG Helicopter 6512 observed a localized 150-yard plume dissipating in the channel. Acid mist tracks North-Northwest at 8 mph; runoff moves East-Southeast on the ebb tide at 1.2 knots. Shoreline impacts are confined to 400 yards of bulkhead and piling. Show Staging Area Bravo, Boom Site 1, the Sector Houston-Galveston Command Post, the 1,000-foot Exclusion Zone, and navigation safety zones.
5 Situation Summary and Health and Safet: At 10:50, a high-pressure discharge hose burst during offloading and spilled approximately 4,200 gallons of 98% sulfuric acid. An exothermic reaction with bilge water produced a dense corrosive mist. Hazards include severe skin necrosis, permanent ocular damage, pulmonary edema from inhalation, extreme heat when acid mixes with water, and slips on degraded decking. Enforce a 1,000-foot Exclusion Zone; require Level A chemical suits with SCBA for Hot Zone entry and Level B with SCBA for Warm Zone support; continuously sample water pH and monitor acid mist; and use a mandatory dual-stage lime-neutralization decontamination wash at Gate 4.
7 Current and Planned Objectives: Enforce the 1,000-foot Exclusion Zone and secure vessel offloading by 12:00; neutralize the deck spill with sodium bicarbonate slurry by 14:00; deploy a chemical-neutralization boom at Berth 42 by 13:30; monitor acid mist along the Channelview perimeter by 15:00; and transition to Unified Command by 12:30.
ActionsRow1: Port Authority Fire Engines 81 and 82 responded and established a 1,000-foot safety perimeter.
ActionsRow2: Captain H. Vance established Sector Command and restricted Houston Ship Channel traffic to one-way slow speed.
ActionsRow3: Port Hazmat Team 1 arrived, established a pH-monitoring grid, and set up the neutralization decontamination corridor.
ActionsRow4: The USCG Strike Team arrived and initiated shipboard inspection and a containment audit.
ActionsRow5: The Stolt Tankers RP response vessel deployed chemical sorbent boom around M/T Stolt Synergy.
ActionsRow6: Entry Team Alpha in Level A PPE executes emergency valve shutdown on the shipboard manifold.
ActionsRow7: Begin high-volume sodium bicarbonate dry-powder application on the vessel deck.
ActionsRow8: Perform a secondary overflight to confirm complete plume dissipation.
